subject: C07
required_fixes: R1 (high) — .inputs/academy/src/features/labs/desktop/use-desktop-draft.ts:91,98,109 and unmount cleanup: device serialization belongs to each hook instance, so it ends at the wrong lifetime boundary. Independently reproduced: view 1 writes A with its acknowledgement delayed, edits B and unmounts; view 2 edits and keeps C, then unmounts; releasing view 1's acknowledgement lets its queued B overwrite C. Reopening restores B, with no network calls. Serialize or version device operations for the account/attempt across successive mounts, including reads, clears and retired views' pending operations. Acceptance: that exact sequence recovers C; delayed writes/clears from old views cannot replace or delete newer work, and account retirement still prevents cross-account access.

R2 (high) — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/offline_domain.rs:737,819: revalidation is not bound to the record observation it started with. Courses compare only the authored revision, so removal followed by a same-revision re-download can receive an obsolete verdict. Attempts are replaced unconditionally whenever the record still exists: an older delayed unlocked reply can overwrite a newer cached revision-withdrawn lock or a newer draftVersion, renewing cachedAt in the process. Bind asynchronous revalidation to a record generation/observation and reject superseded results, including foreground-cache writes and overlapping revalidations. Acceptance: delayed revalidation cannot undo a same-revision re-download, replace a newer locked attempt with an older unlocked one, or regress a newer saved draft; verify offline reads and restart after each race.

R3 (high) — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/offline_domain.rs:499,534,560,723: offline authorization uses the in-memory index, while course revalidation updates files and refreshes that index only after every cached-attempt revalidation finishes. During a delayed unrelated attempt request, a course already persisted as withdrawn remains readable: answer checks the old index and then returns content from the withdrawn record without checking that record's status/lease. Concurrent rebuilds can also publish older index snapshots out of order. Make serving decisions against current authoritative record state and publish withdrawal promptly without waiting for unrelated checks; prevent stale index publication from reviving access. Acceptance: after a course denial is persisted, hold attempt revalidation and force a unit/lab network failure; neither content nor an unlocked cached attempt for that withdrawn course is exposed, including with overlapping rebuilds.

R4 (high) — crates/desktop-core/src/offline.rs:183,327,362 and authority/offline_domain.rs:434: any 32-byte key opens an existing store. With the wrong key, rebuilding lists treats every valid encrypted record as corrupt, renames them, and now automatically deletes all but the newest eight. The existing wrong-key test exercises only one record and therefore misses irreversible loss of legitimate drafts. This contradicts the documented closed, non-writing wrong-key behavior. Authenticate the existing store/key before destructive recovery or pruning, and preserve valid encrypted user work when the key cannot be verified. Acceptance: seed more than eight valid course/draft records, reopen through the production path with another 32-byte key, and prove unavailable status with no deleted or rewritten work; restoring the original key recovers every record.

R5 (medium) — .inputs/academy/src/features/labs/desktop/use-desktop-draft.ts:109,188; use-desktop-attempt.ts:36,42; crates/desktop-core/src/authority/learner_domain.rs:1210 and offline_domain.rs:613: confirming a save clears the device copy, but successful draft-save/resolve mutations neither advance the persisted attempt's draft/version nor require a successful attempt refresh. The only native cache updates come from attempt queries. Consequently online editing can leave v0 in the attempt cache, save v1 successfully, clear its local copy, and then reopen offline with v0/empty work. An independent hook probe reproduced that reopen using the unchanged last cached attempt; provider and mutation-hook inspection found no intervening invalidation/readback. Preserve the last confirmed learner work for offline continuity before clearing its sole current local copy, without extending content leases or inventing grading truth. Acceptance: save and resolve work online, prevent any later attempt.get from succeeding, restart offline, and recover the confirmed draft/version without automatic submission.

R6 (medium) — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/offline_domain.rs:1042 and the draft hook's one-time load effect: load_draft returns successful null whenever generation.store is None, including while existing protected work is still opening. The hook then never reloads when opening completes. A lab opened online during slow startup/decryption can therefore show the server draft and miss the newer device draft; a subsequent edit can overwrite that unseen copy. Join the existing-store opening operation or return a distinct pending/unavailable result that the host handles without declaring absence. Acceptance: delay opening an account with a saved local draft, open its lab while online, then release opening; the local work is restored or explicitly reconciled, never silently treated as missing, with reset/sign-out retirement still respected.
evidence_gaps: E1 follow-up — tools/native-acceptance/academy_offline.py:55 now uses correctly bounded 6 MiB parts, and native evidence confirms stopping after three parts with no retained download. However each successful unitBundle response still contains only revision/units/labs. The pinned bundles.ts returns the complete bundle projection, including schemaVersion, courseId, accountId, manifest, lease and the remaining metadata. Attempt-01 explicitly requested complete contract-valid projections; this portion remains unmet. Build the overflow fixture from that actual shape, assert every serialized part stays below Academy's 7 MiB cap, and repeat the source-bound native overflow evidence.
optional_suggestions: Downloads shows only a count of local drafts and says to open their labs. Consider listing recognizable lab/course labels and direct reopening actions so learners can find saved work without remembering its location.

Remediation makes substantial progress: the original single-view R3 latest-edit sequence and R4 delayed-load sequence now pass independent production-hook probes. Source and recorded tests support the reset write ledger, serialized commits with owned temporary files, bounded/counting quarantine, aggregate assembly limit and ordinary attempt lease/lock handling. Original E2 is resolved: the common 57-test library log explicitly records an_interrupted_write_leaves_the_previous_version passing, including its reopen assertions.

Ran four independent in-memory React/JSDOM probes using the actual pinned draft hook. Two confirmed original fixes; one reproduced newer work being overwritten across successive mounts; one demonstrated the confirmed-save/old-offline-attempt continuity gap. The latter supplies the stale attempt that source inspection establishes the native cache retains. These are scripted boundaries, not a native-window or full Rust-store execution.

Rust findings about late revalidation, stale authorization indexes, wrong-key pruning and loading during opening are source-path/interleaving analyses. Did not run filesystem-writing Rust tests or resource/race probes because this review permits writes only to its verdict. Reviewed the actual new tests and their source-bound logs instead.
